## Executive Summary

For **Week 18 (2026-04-27 to 2026-05-03)**, the national incidence of
acute respiratory infection reached **142 cases per 100,000**, nearly
three times the epidemic threshold of 50. Incidence has now stayed above
threshold for four consecutive weeks. The time-varying reproduction number
**R(t) = 1.42** (95% CI 1.28–1.58) indicates sustained transmission with a
doubling time of roughly nine days.

Transmission is geographically concentrated: the **Riverdale Metropolitan
Area** alone accounts for 38% of the national caseload. Children aged 0–4
carry the highest age-specific rate. Influenza A (H1N1) dominates the
laboratory-confirmed mix.

## Background

The Riverdale sentinel surveillance network comprises **501 reporting
sites** — primary-care clinics, emergency departments, and four reference
laboratories — covering an estimated 64% of the national population.
Sites report syndromic counts daily and submit a sampling fraction for
laboratory confirmation. Population denominators are drawn from the 2025
mid-year civil registry.

The epidemic threshold of 50 per 100,000 is the upper bound of the
Serfling-model baseline computed over the five preceding non-epidemic
seasons. Crossing it triggers this enhanced weekly bulletin.

## Methods

- **Case definition.** ICD-10 J09–J18 (influenza and pneumonia) with
  symptom onset in the reporting week.
- **Surveillance type.** Passive syndromic reporting plus an active
  laboratory-confirmation arm at the four reference labs.
- **R(t) estimation.** Cori et al. instantaneous method over a sliding
  7-day window, assuming a serial interval of mean 3.6 days (SD 1.8).
- **Denominators.** 2025 civil-registry mid-year population, stratified
  by the four standard age bands.

## Data

The weekly incidence series below is the raw input for every figure in
this bulletin. The full eighteen-week record lives in
`data/weekly_cases.csv`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-recent
#| tbl-cap: "Most recent eight weeks of national surveillance data"
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

cases = pd.read_csv("data/weekly_cases.csv")
recent = cases.tail(8).copy()
recent["over_threshold"] = recent["cases_per_100k"] > recent["threshold"]
recent = recent.rename(columns={
    "week": "Wk",
    "cases_per_100k": "Cases/100k",
    "threshold": "Threshold",
    "r_t": "R(t)",
    "hospitalizations": "Hosp.",
    "deaths": "Deaths",
    "over_threshold": "Above thr.",
})
recent
```

The epidemic curve makes the threshold breach and the sustained climb
explicit. The dashed line marks the epidemic threshold; the shaded span
highlights the four weeks of continuous exceedance.

```{python}
#| label: fig-epicurve
#| fig-cap: "Epidemic curve — weekly incidence vs. epidemic threshold (cases per 100k)"
#| code-fold: true
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

over = cases[cases["cases_per_100k"] > cases["threshold"]]
breach_start = int(over["week"].iloc[0]) if not over.empty else None

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
ax1.bar(cases["week"], cases["cases_per_100k"],
        color="#c0392b", alpha=0.85, label="Cases/100k")
ax1.axhline(50, ls="--", color="#34495e", label="Epidemic threshold")
if breach_start is not None:
    ax1.axvspan(14.5, 18.5, color="#f39c12", alpha=0.12,
                label="4 weeks above threshold")
ax1.set_xlabel("Epidemiological week")
ax1.set_ylabel("Cases per 100,000")

ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.plot(cases["week"], cases["r_t"], color="#2c3e50",
         marker="o", ms=3, label="R(t)")
ax2.axhline(1.0, ls=":", color="#7f8c8d")
ax2.set_ylabel("R(t)")
ax2.set_ylim(0.8, 1.6)

ax1.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Incidence and R(t) rise together through the season; R(t) never returns
below the containment line of 1.0.

## Results

### Age stratification

| Age group | Cases per 100k | Year-over-year |
|-----------|---------------:|---------------:|
| 0–4       | 198            | +24%           |
| 5–17      | 156            | +18%           |
| 18–64     | 132            | +14%           |
| 65+       | 122            | +9%            |

Children aged 0–4 are disproportionately affected, consistent with
school- and daycare-driven transmission early in the wave.

### Geographic distribution

| Region                  | Cases/100k | Status        |
|-------------------------|-----------:|---------------|
| Riverdale Metropolitan  | 198        | exceeded ⚠    |
| Greenfield County       | 168        | exceeded ⚠    |
| Bayside District        | 134        | exceeded ⚠    |
| Dunmore Region          | 102        | exceeded ⚠    |
| All other regions       | 88         | approaching   |

### Etiology

Among laboratory-confirmed specimens this week: **Influenza A (H1N1) 63%**,
RSV 22%, SARS-CoV-2 9%, and other respiratory viruses 6%. The H1N1
dominance is unchanged from Week 16.

## Discussion

Four consecutive weeks above threshold, an R(t) holding near 1.4, and a
nine-day doubling time together describe an outbreak that is still
expanding rather than plateauing. The age profile — heaviest in the
under-fives — points to schools and daycare as primary amplifiers, while
the concentration in the Riverdale Metropolitan Area suggests a
metropolitan seeding event that has not yet fully diffused outward.

Hospitalizations have risen broadly in step with incidence (see the data
table), but the case-fatality count remains low, consistent with a
seasonal H1N1 signature rather than a novel-strain emergence.

## Recommendations

1. **Vaccination push** — current 65+ uptake is 47%; target 70% by Wk 20.
2. **School advisory** — enhanced hygiene and symptomatic isolation in the
   Riverdale Metropolitan Area and Greenfield County.
3. **Hospital surge readiness** — national ICU reserve sits at 12%; trigger
   the surge plan if Week 19 incidence exceeds 160 per 100,000.

## Limitations

Passive syndromic reporting under-ascertains mild cases, so the true
incidence is higher than reported. Laboratory confirmation covers only a
sampling fraction, and the R(t) estimate is sensitive to the assumed serial
interval. Regional denominators predate the 2026 census update.
